subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Obtain the reduction formula for I_n = ∫ sinⁿx dx, n being a positive integer, n ≥ 2, and hence find ∫ sin⁴x dx.

mark_split.label: Apply by parts and use sin²x = 1 − cos²x
Substitute n = 4, 2, 0 for the final answer

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book printed p.26 (PDF page 25) — LAQ chapter 3 ‘Integration’, sub-head INTEGRATION-I, answer 16.1, on a ★★★ SSP page (book p.26, per the survey's SSP list). Printed appearances: TS 18,20 · AP 15,17,19. Chapter star rank ★★★ (book p.13). no printed margin mark tags or tick-box splits appear anywhere in the Integration LAQ chapter (book pp.26-37) — this card's mark split is OURS, patterned on the 7-mark shapes printed elsewhere in the book (e.g. 2+2+2+1, 1+1+2+2+1). Where this book is wrong: the book's own final printed line drops the leading minus sign it carries on the line immediately above it — it prints ‘= sin³x cosx/4 − 3/8 sinx cosx + 3/8 x + c’ for the last line, while the line right before it correctly carries ‘−sin³x cosx/4’. Differentiating the printed (unsigned) form does NOT return sin⁴x, while differentiating −sin³x cosx/4 − 3/8 sinx cosx + 3/8 x + c does — this card keeps the correct minus sign, carried through consistently from the line above it, and records the book's likely typo here. This finding is this unit's own (the task-flagged suspect is answer 18.2, a different, confirmed instance of the same slip). No two-book union check and no board back-test were possible for Maths-2B (no second-year TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand; the book's five Guess Papers pp.118-127 stand in for the back-test).

insider_note: Put n = 4, 2, 0 one after another and stop as soon as you reach I₀ = x — substituting n = 4 directly into the n, n−2 formula without first working out I₂ is the most common way this method mark is lost.

steps.label: Set up integration by parts
lines: Given I_n = ∫ sinⁿx dx = ∫ sinⁿ⁻¹x · sinx dx
Take first function u = sinⁿ⁻¹x, second v = sinx
steps.why: A reduction formula always comes from integration by parts applied to the earlier power, peeling off one factor of sinx so what remains inside the new integral is one power lower.
common_mistakes: Taking u = sinx and v = sinⁿ⁻¹x the wrong way round, which does not simplify on differentiation.
Forgetting the integration constant when writing ∫v dx = −cosx at this stage (it cancels later, but skipping it is bad form).
steps.memory_tip: Split off ONE sinx as the part you integrate (dv); the leftover sinⁿ⁻¹x is the part you differentiate (u).

steps.label: Apply by parts and use sin²x = 1 − cos²x
steps.why: Replacing cos²x by 1 − sin²x turns the new integral back into powers of sinx alone, which is exactly ∫sinⁿ⁻²x dx and ∫sinⁿx dx — the two integrals the reduction formula must relate.
common_mistakes: Leaving cos²x un-replaced, which never leads back to I_n or I_{n−2}.
Sign slip when distributing the double negative in −∫sinⁿ⁻²x cosx(−cosx)dx.
steps.memory_tip: cos²x = 1 − sin²x is the ONLY substitution that closes the loop back to I_n.

steps.label: Solve for the reduction formula
steps.why: Collecting every I_n term on the left and dividing by n turns the identity into a genuine recursion — the n-th integral written using only the (n−2)-th one, which is what ‘reduction’ means.
common_mistakes: Dividing by (n−1) instead of n when isolating I_n.
Stopping at nI_n = … without dividing through, so the boxed formula is left with a stray n.
steps.memory_tip: n on the LEFT of I_n = …, always. Say it as ‘n copies of I_n equal…, so divide by n’.

steps.label: Substitute n = 4, 2, 0 for the final answer
steps.why: Each substitution of n needs the PREVIOUS even case, so n = 4 needs I₂, and I₂ needs I₀ = x — climbing back down the chain of even n is what finally removes every I from the answer.
common_mistakes: Stopping at I₄ = −sin³x cosx/4 + (3/4)I₂ without substituting the value of I₂.
Losing the leading minus sign on −sin³x cosx/4 when copying the boxed formula's result into the final line.
steps.memory_tip: Even n chains down to I₀ = x; odd n would chain down to I₁ = −cosx instead.
